newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba plays down EU-U.S. Helms-Burton deal.
newsitem.headline: Cuba plays down EU-U.S. Helms-Burton deal.

text.p: Cuba said on Tuesday that recent moves by the U.S. and the European Union to defuse a trade dispute over the U.S. Helms-Burton law were not significant and it repeated its call for the entire law to be scrapped.

Foreign Investment Minister Ibrahim Ferradaz said the understanding reached earlier this month between U.S. and European negotiators did not change the basic thrust of the U.S. law, which he condemned as a hostile "annexionist platform" aimed against Cuba.
"It does not substantally modify the situation," he said at a foreign investment seminar in Havana. "We say that this law is an attack (against Cuba) and that the whole law should be revoked."
He added that the U.S.-EU deal appeared to him to be more of an understanding than a formal agreement.

Earlier in April, the European Commission announced it had struck a deal with the U.S. government under which the EU agreed to suspend an initiative to take its dispute over the U.S. Helms-Burton law to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

The U.S. legislation, introduced one year ago, threatens penalties against foreign investors in Cuba judged to be "trafficking" in expropriated, formerly U.S.-owned properties on the island. It also called on Cuba to dump its president, Fidel Castro, and to abandon one-party communist rule.

Under the recent deal, ratified by EU members, President Bill Clinton said he would continue to suspend application of a key clause of the Helms-Burton law and would also seek permission from Congress to modify another clause. The EU and the U.S. would try to draw up international guidelines on how to treat investment involving illegally expropriated property.

Ferradaz said that none of the foreign investors who had already been operating in Cuba prior to the Helms-Burton law had withdrawn because of the legislation. But he acknowledged that the law may have frightened off potential new investors and had also affected the flow of credits to the island.
